slides.heading: Nested for Loops
slides.body: Nested for Loops is part of Definite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Nested for Loops
slides.body: A nested for loop places one loop inside another. It is commonly used for grids, tables, and repeated patterns.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Nested loops are like rows and seats in a classroom. For each row, you check each seat.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use for loops when you want to repeat through a known range or sequence.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use nested loops to print row and column pairs for a 2 by 2 grid.
slides.hint: Inside the row loop, add a column loop and print row, col.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create a nested loop that prints two rows and three columns as pairs.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
